Many of us inhabit bodies and faces that don’t look as we feel they should. It’s one of the most painful aspects of being human. Here are a few minutes of consolation and wisdom.

Be more mindful, present and inspired. Get the best of The School of Life delivered straight to your inbox: https://t.ly/PbPmj

FURTHER READING

“Frustration with one’s appearance is an embarrassing – but, in truth, highly serious and valid – pain. Mature, reasonable people are not supposed to go around regretting their nose or hair. Yet you gaze in the bathroom mirror and think: why – in my brief existence on this planet – does that have to be me?...”

author: The School of Life
description:
We often get anxious about the state of our memories—forgetting a item at the store or blanking on an acquaintance's name mid-conversation. But before we lament our faulty minds, we should realize how much we owe to them. Start your free Membership trial – 2,000+ articles, 1,000+ videos, 50+ courses, free for a week: https://www.theschooloflife.com/membership 

If our memories were truly infallible, we would be haunted by the perfection of lost moments and forced to howl in continuous heartbreak. In this film, we explore how forgetting is not a failure, but a quiet, merciful design that allows us to heal and survive.

"We can get very anxious indeed about the state of our memories. Last week, we forgot about buying a new head for the mop. Recently, mid-way through a conversation with Albert, we realised we couldn’t summon up his name. There are drawbacks for sure, but before we start to lament them too much, we should remember just how much we ultimately owe to these faulty instrument
